title: Two ways software reaches a board

steps.title: The boot ROM decides how you flash
steps.body:
Which model you get is decided by the silicon vendor's boot ROM and tooling, not by you. Everything else in the stack is the same.

Left is the SD-card image model, right is the vendor-flash model.

steps.title: SD-card model: build pieces, make one image
steps.body:
Used by the i.MX 8M Plus and the STM32MP257F-DK. `./build.sh all` builds the boot firmware, U-Boot, kernel and rootfs into `build/deploy/`, and `image.sh` assembles ONE disk image with the bootloader at a fixed offset.

The PC only needs a card reader.

steps.anchor: Write the image to an SD card
steps.title: Flash, move the card, flip the switch
steps.body:
`./build.sh flash` writes the card, then you set the boot switch to SD and power on. The Boot ROM reads the card by itself: ROM, firmware, U-Boot, Linux, all from the card.

The serial console is at 115200.

steps.anchor: Fix a mistake: re-flash the card. The ROM runs first, so a bad card cannot brick it.
steps.title: A bad card cannot brick the board
steps.body: The ROM runs before anything on the card, so re-flashing always recovers.

steps.title: Vendor-flash model: start from the vendor's package
steps.body: Used by the Jetson Orin Nano and many QSPI/eMMC-only SoCs. `./build.sh fetch` downloads the vendor's board support package (signed boot firmware, flashing tools, sample rootfs), and you add your kernel, device tree and rootfs changes into its staging tree.

steps.anchor: Put the board in recovery mode
steps.title: Recovery mode makes the ROM wait for the host
steps.body:
A jumper or button plus a USB cable puts the Boot ROM in a state where it waits for the host (`lsusb` shows it). The vendor tool then flashes boot firmware into on-board flash and the OS into SD, NVMe or eMMC.

After a reboot the firmware lives in the board's own flash, not on a card.

steps.anchor: Fix a mistake: flash again. Recovery mode lives in the ROM (until you burn fuses).
steps.title: Recovery stays available until fuses are burned
steps.body: Flash again to fix a mistake, because recovery mode is in the ROM. Burning fuses is what can remove that way back.

steps.anchor: Why it matters: the SD-card model lets you iterate with one cheap card and see the whole build as one image. The vendor-flash model needs a Linux x86-64 host
steps.title: Takeaway: cheap iteration vs. signed firmware
steps.body: The SD-card model lets you iterate with one cheap card. The vendor-flash model needs a Linux x86-64 host and vendor tools, but the firmware sits in on-board flash, so it can be signed and updated separately from the OS storage.
